Noise cancelling headphones are, in effect, very sophisticated microphones. That's because the headphones must listen constantly to the acoustic environment around them and then send it in the opposite direction – over into the environment of the device wearing the headphones. This involves the device’s software using extremely complex algorithms and advanced technology to cancel and reverse specific frequencies in the audio.
A good noise cancelling headphone or earbud will cancel noise within a 30-degree range. This means the headphone will cancel noise that's coming from the left, right, front, back and other angles.
The reason the headphones can cancel noise in this way is because they are essentially microphones. The microphone of a noise cancelling headphone is responsible for detecting the noise and sending it back in the opposite direction – or reversing – into the environment of the headphone wearer. This reversal of the noise can then be effectively cancelled.
Of course, the microphones used in noise cancelling headphones must be highly sensitive and accurate if they are going to work properly. They must be designed to accurately detect frequency and sound that is going on either side – and the microphone of a good noise cancelling headphone must have such precision. If the headphones are unable to hear the noise of the environment around them – for whatever reason – then it's going to be nearly impossible for them to cancel that noise effectively.
